mechanism_claims.claim_text: Peptides of at least 10 amino acids bind anionic membranes as beta-strands and self-assemble in the bilayer, causing membrane permeabilization in MIC, hemolysis, and vesicle leakage assays.

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper supports membranolytic activity and self-assembly but does not resolve a single atomic pore structure.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KL10, KL14, and KL18 peptides in phosphate-containing solution
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Phosphate ions promote amyloid-like beta-sheet fibril/ribbon aggregation in solution, reducing available monomeric peptide and lowering apparent antimicrobial or leakage activity when peptides are pre-exposed to phosphate.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: KL6 binds anionic vesicles but is too short to form beta-sheets or produce meaningful membranolytic activity under the tested conditions.
